gap: No result ChatGPT got states, apart from a footnote on Anker's own product page that none of the answers or comparison pages used, that Anker guarantees the Prime 160W's single-port 140 W without derating only 'for at least 1 hour in 100 - 130V areas' (US outlets), while it never derates at 220–240 V, and that its 2-minute dynamic power reallocation works only in AI Mode 2.0.
standout_why: I checked our own page, itechguides (cited), Notebookcheck's US launch news (cited), the Notebookcheck review (cited once) and Anker's US product page (cited in 4 of 5 chats). itechguides says nothing about derating or AI Mode reallocation. Notebookcheck covers only the UGREEN. Our page has adamtalks' measurement (about 110 W after 20–25 min) and the replug pause, but not Anker's own 120 V vs 230 V wording. The finding is on anker.com, which ChatGPT cited, but it sits in a footnote and every ChatGPT answer said thermals were undecided. So rivals have part of it, not none of it.
decides: It backs the pick rather than changing it. For a US shopper who runs a 16-inch MacBook Pro at full 140 W for long stretches, Anker itself only promises un-derated output for at least one hour on 120 V, and its smart splitting needs AI Mode 2.0, with Dual-Laptop Mode only through the app. So the Anker's edge is size and weight for travel, not sustained desk power. The UGREEN stays the desk pick, but its own limit should be stated: 140 W only on C1/C2, C3 is a PD 3.0 port capped at 100 W, and the laptop port drops to 65 W once 4–5 devices are connected.

findings.label: Single-port derating by mains voltage (maker footnote 1)
findings.value: At 77°F: no derating at 220–240 V; without derating 'for at least 1 hour' at 100–130 V
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Exact wording: '1. At 77°F, single-port charging runs without derating in 220 - 240V areas, and for at least 1 hour in 100 - 130V areas.' US outlets are 120 V, so that is the derating case. Anker gives no figure for what happens after the hour.

findings.label: Dynamic power distribution: mode needed and interval
findings.value: Reallocates every 2 minutes, only in AI Mode 2.0
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: Quotes: 'Auto-detects and reallocates power every 2 minutes for optimal charging.' 'Dynamic power distribution is only available in AI Mode 2.0.' 'Dual-Laptop Mode is enabled in the app after connecting via Bluetooth.' The page gives no per-port split for Standard Mode, only '160W Max' for two or three ports.

findings.label: Single-port output and 150 W condition
findings.value: 28V⎓5A (140 W) on any of C1/C2/C3; 28V⎓5.36A (150 W) only in AI Mode with Anker Prime Power Bank A110A and listed Anker 240 W cables
findings.source_title: Why can't the single-port output of Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) reach 150W? - Anker Support
findings.note: The compatible device list names only the A110A power bank. Cables: A88E2, A82E2, A84N1 or the cable that comes with the A110A.

findings.label: Conditions for reaching 140 W on a MacBook
findings.value: M1/M2 MacBook Pro: USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable only; M3/M4: EPR USB-C or MagSafe 3; power drops automatically above 80% battery
findings.source_title: Why can't the single-port output of Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) reach 140W? - Anker Support
findings.note: Anker's wording: 'Both the charger and the device must support 140W to reach the maximum output.' The same cable rule applies to any 140 W PD 3.1 charger, including the UGREEN.

findings.source_title: Anker Prime Charger (160W, 3 Ports, Smart Display) - Anker US
findings.note: The page also shows 'Save $34.00' and a 10+ unit bulk price of $102.05. Weight 220 g; 65 × 52 × 35 mm without prongs.

findings.label: Per-port maximum and protocol, measured with an FNB58 tester
findings.source_title: One charger for almost everything: 5-port Ugreen Nexode Pro 160W review - Notebookcheck Review
findings.note: So a laptop plugged into C3 can never get more than 100 W. With a laptop on C1 and four other devices for 1 hour, Notebookcheck measured 56–58 W at C1. The review gives no derating data.

findings.label: Laptop-port output as more devices are added
findings.value: 100 W held on one USB-C port with up to 3 devices; 65 W with 4 or 5 devices
findings.source_title: Ugreen's new 5-port 160W charger with display launches in the US - Notebookcheck News
findings.note: This restates UGREEN's claims. A cited rival already has it, so it is context only, not the gap.
